13.2.5 Effect of Heat on Nitrates, Carbonates and Hydrogen-Carbonates explaining the Trend in Terms of the Polarizing Ability of the Positive Ion

Compounds of Group – IA elements are more stable to heat than the corresponding compounds of Group – IIA elements with the exception of lithium compounds.

Effect of Heat on Nitrates

In Group – IA the lithium nitrates decomposes on the same way as the nitrates of Group – IIA. Group – IIA nitrates tend to decompose on heating to produce metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide (brown fumes) and oxygen.

Tidbit

The ability of a cation to distort an anion is known as its polarization power and the tendency of the anion to become polarized by the cation is known as its polarizability.

Lithium nitrate on decomposition produces lithium oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

4LiNO₃(s) —Δ→ 2Li₂O(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g)

The rest of nitrates from sodium to caesium, however, do not decompose completely at low temperatures. At high temperature, the nitrates of these elements produce the respective metal nitrite (MNO₂) and oxygen, but no nitrogen dioxide. (Where M = Na, K, Rb and Cs)

2MNO₃(s) —Δ→ 2MNO₂(s) + O₂(g)

As we go down the group, the decomposition of these metal nitrates becomes more difficult and higher temperature is required.

Effect of Heat on Carbonates

In Group – IA the lithium carbonate decomposes on the same way as the carbonates of Group – IIA. Group – IIA carbonates tend to decompose on heating to produce metal oxide and carbon dioxide.

In Group – IA, lithium carbonate behaves in the same way, producing lithium oxide and carbon dioxide

Li₂CO₃(s) → Li₂O(s) + CO₂(g)

The rest of the Group – IA carbonates do not decompose at low temperature, although at higher temperature this becomes possible. The decomposition temperatures again increase down the group.

Effect of Heat on Hydrogen Carbonates

The hydrogen carbonates of Group – IA are stable enough to exist as solid, although they do decompose easily on heating. For example,

2NaHCO₃(s) → Na₂CO₃(s) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(g)

Explaining the Trend in Terms of the Polarizing ability of the Positive Ion

A small positive ion has a large amount of charge packed into a small volume of space. An ion with a high charge density has a clear distorting effect on any nearby negative ions. A larger positive ion has the same charge spread over a larger volume of space. Its charge density is therefore lower and it causes less distortion to nearby negative ions.

Polarizing the Carbonate ion

The molecular structure of carbonate is given below:

This figure shows two carbon-oxygen single bonds and one double bond, with two oxygen atoms each carrying a negative charge.

In carbonate, bonds are identical and the charges are delocalized.

The positive ion attracts the delocalized electrons in the carbonate ion towards itself. The carbonate ion becomes polarized.

Figure 13.2 Molecular structure of carbonate.

When it is heated, the carbon dioxide gets free, leaving a metal oxide. The amount of heat required depends on the polarization of the ion. If the positive ion has only one positive charge, the polarizing effect is reduced. This is why the Group – IA compounds are more thermally stable than those in Group – IIA.

په IA ګروپ کې لیتیم نایټرېټ د IIA ګروپ د نایټرېټونو په څېر تجزیه کېږي. د IIA ګروپ نایټرېټونه د تودولو پر مهال د فلزي اکسایډ، نایټروجن ډای اکسایډ (نسواري لوګیو) او اکسیجن د جوړولو تمایل لري.

لنډ معلومات

د مثبت ایون هغه وړتیا چې منفي ایون کږوي، د هغه د قطبي کولو ځواک بلل کېږي؛ او د مثبت ایون له خوا د منفي ایون د قطبي کېدو تمایل د هغه قطبي کېدونکې وړتیا بلل کېږي.

لیتیم نایټرېټ په تجزیه کې لیتیم اکسایډ، نایټروجن ډای اکسایډ او اکسیجن جوړوي.

4LiNO₃(s) —Δ→ 2Li₂O(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g)

خو له سوډیم څخه سیزیم پورې پاتې نایټرېټونه په ټیټه تودوخه کې بشپړ نه تجزیه کېږي. په لوړه تودوخه کې د دې عناصرو نایټرېټونه اړوند فلزي نایټرایټ (MNO₂) او اکسیجن جوړوي، خو نایټروجن ډای اکسایډ نه جوړوي. (چې M = Na، K، Rb او Cs دی)

2MNO₃(s) —Δ→ 2MNO₂(s) + O₂(g)

په ګروپ کې ښکته تګ سره د دې فلزي نایټرېټونو تجزیه ستونزمنېږي او لوړه تودوخه اړینه وي.

پر کاربونېټونو د تودوخې اغېز

په IA ګروپ کې لیتیم کاربونېټ د IIA ګروپ د کاربونېټونو په څېر تجزیه کېږي. د IIA ګروپ کاربونېټونه په تودولو سره د فلزي اکسایډ او کاربن ډای اکسایډ د جوړولو تمایل لري.

په IA ګروپ کې لیتیم کاربونېټ په همدې ډول چلند کوي او لیتیم اکسایډ او کاربن ډای اکسایډ جوړوي.

Li₂CO₃(s) → Li₂O(s) + CO₂(g)

د IA ګروپ پاتې کاربونېټونه په ټیټه تودوخه کې نه تجزیه کېږي، خو په لوړه تودوخه کې دا ممکنه کېږي. په ګروپ کې ښکته تګ سره د تجزیې تودوخې بیا لوړېږي.

پر هایدروجن کاربونېټونو د تودوخې اغېز

د IA ګروپ هایدروجن کاربونېټونه دومره ثابت دي چې په جامد حالت کې موجودېدای شي، خو په تودولو سره په اسانه تجزیه کېږي. د بېلګې په توګه:

2NaHCO₃(s) → Na₂CO₃(s) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(g)

د مثبت ایون د قطبي کولو د وړتیا له مخې د تمایل تشریح

په یوه کوچني مثبت ایون کې په لږ حجم کې ډېر چارج راټول وي. د لوړ چارج کثافت لرونکی ایون پر نږدې منفي ایونونو څرګند کږوونکی اغېز لري. لوی مثبت ایون هماغه چارج په لوی حجم کې خپور لري؛ نو د چارج کثافت یې ټیټ او پر نږدې منفي ایونونو د کږولو اغېز یې لږ وي.

د کاربونېټ ایون قطبي کول

د کاربونېټ مالیکولي جوړښت لاندې ورکړل شوی دی:

دا شکل د کاربن او اکسیجن دوه واحد تړونونه او یو دوه ګونی تړون ښيي؛ د اکسیجن دوه اټومونه هر یو منفي چارج لري.

په کاربونېټ کې تړونونه یو شان دي او چارجونه غیرموضعي دي.

مثبت ایون په کاربونېټ ایون کې غیرموضعي الکترونونه ځان ته راکاږي او کاربونېټ ایون قطبي کېږي.

شکل 13.2 د کاربونېټ مالیکولي جوړښت.

په تودولو سره کاربن ډای اکسایډ ازادېږي او فلزي اکسایډ پاتې کېږي. د اړینې تودوخې مقدار د ایون په قطبي کېدو پورې اړه لري. که مثبت ایون یوازې یو مثبت چارج ولري، د قطبي کولو اغېز کمېږي. له همدې امله د IA ګروپ مرکبات د IIA ګروپ له مرکباتو ډېر حرارتي ثبات لري.

13.2.5 Effect of Heat on Nitrates, Carbonates and Hydrogen-Carbonates explaining the Trend in Terms of the Polarizing Ability of the Positive Ion

Compounds of Group – IA elements are more stable to heat than the corresponding compounds of Group – IIA elements with the exception of lithium compounds.

Effect of Heat on Nitrates

In Group – IA the lithium nitrates decomposes on the same way as the nitrates of Group – IIA. Group – IIA nitrates tend to decompose on heating to produce metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide (brown fumes) and oxygen.

Tidbit

The ability of a cation to distort an anion is known as its polarization power and the tendency of the anion to become polarized by the cation is known as its polarizability.

Lithium nitrate on decomposition produces lithium oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

4LiNO₃(s) —Δ→ 2Li₂O(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g)

The rest of nitrates from sodium to caesium, however, do not decompose completely at low temperatures. At high temperature, the nitrates of these elements produce the respective metal nitrite (MNO₂) and oxygen, but no nitrogen dioxide. (Where M = Na, K, Rb and Cs)

2MNO₃(s) —Δ→ 2MNO₂(s) + O₂(g)

As we go down the group, the decomposition of these metal nitrates becomes more difficult and higher temperature is required.

Effect of Heat on Carbonates

In Group – IA the lithium carbonate decomposes on the same way as the carbonates of Group – IIA. Group – IIA carbonates tend to decompose on heating to produce metal oxide and carbon dioxide.

In Group – IA, lithium carbonate behaves in the same way, producing lithium oxide and carbon dioxide

Li₂CO₃(s) → Li₂O(s) + CO₂(g)

The rest of the Group – IA carbonates do not decompose at low temperature, although at higher temperature this becomes possible. The decomposition temperatures again increase down the group.

Effect of Heat on Hydrogen Carbonates

The hydrogen carbonates of Group – IA are stable enough to exist as solid, although they do decompose easily on heating. For example,

2NaHCO₃(s) → Na₂CO₃(s) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(g)

Explaining the Trend in Terms of the Polarizing ability of the Positive Ion

A small positive ion has a large amount of charge packed into a small volume of space. An ion with a high charge density has a clear distorting effect on any nearby negative ions. A larger positive ion has the same charge spread over a larger volume of space. Its charge density is therefore lower and it causes less distortion to nearby negative ions.

Polarizing the Carbonate ion

The molecular structure of carbonate is given below:

This figure shows two carbon-oxygen single bonds and one double bond, with two oxygen atoms each carrying a negative charge.

In carbonate, bonds are identical and the charges are delocalized.

The positive ion attracts the delocalized electrons in the carbonate ion towards itself. The carbonate ion becomes polarized.

Figure 13.2 Molecular structure of carbonate.

When it is heated, the carbon dioxide gets free, leaving a metal oxide. The amount of heat required depends on the polarization of the ion. If the positive ion has only one positive charge, the polarizing effect is reduced. This is why the Group – IA compounds are more thermally stable than those in Group – IIA.
